title: Only the Core Facilitator may impose a ban that would block a governance process, and must publish the reasons
content:
A.2.7.1.2.1.1 gives responsible moderators discretion to ban users "when they deem users to be acting in a misaligned fashion," tempered by a charity default — absent egregious behaviour such as "spamming, flooding, threatening, or using inappropriate or abusive language," they "should err on the side of charity and issue a public warning" first. Then the carve-out: "Only the Core Facilitator may ban a user from the Sky Forum when doing so would operationally block an ongoing governance process (e.g. the user has submitted an otherwise eligible governance proposal)."

The distinction being drawn is between moderation and disenfranchisement. Removing a disruptive participant is housekeeping; removing the participant who has an eligible proposal in flight is a governance act performed through a moderation tool — an attack vector available to whoever holds moderator keys, and a subtle one, since it looks like routine enforcement.

Reserving that specific case to a single named role makes the act attributable, and A.2.7.1.2.1.1.1.1 attaches mandatory transparency to it: the Core Facilitator "must publicly communicate the ban and the reasons for banning a user if the ban interrupts the users' exercise of a governance process," and is responsible for writing the notice.

Elsewhere publicity is discretionary — moderators weigh "the importance of transparency and community awareness" against the user's conduct — but a floor always applies: "In every case, the moderators must still use the built-in forum functionality to register the ban reason for every banned user so that all forum users can see it when visiting the forum profile." Even a quiet ban leaves a reviewable record, so the discretion is over announcement rather than over concealment.
description: Ordinary moderators lose the power precisely where a ban would interrupt someone's exercise of governance, and in that case public communication of the ban and its grounds becomes mandatory.
